title: bot_detection plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `bot_detection` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component BotDetectionConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

BotDetectionConfig.description: Plugin: bot_detection — case-insensitive User-Agent matching. Configuration must be an object and unknown properties are rejected. `blocked_patterns` are substring matches; `allow_list` entries are word-boundary matches and are consulted before blocked patterns, so a User-Agent that contains a blocked substring can still pass if it also contains an allow-list entry as a standalone token (useful for permitting GoogleBot while blocking generic `bot` patterns). The word-boundary anchoring on the allow list prevents an allowed token from being smuggled inside an otherwise-blocked agent. A no-op config (empty `blocked_patterns` while missing User-Agent headers are allowed) is rejected; an allow-list alone is not enforcement. The User-Agent is client-controlled and spoofable, so this is a coarse filter, not strong bot verification. Pattern entry whitespace follows Rust `str::trim` Unicode `White_Space` semantics. A User-Agent whose every field line is empty or only spaces/tabs is treated as missing. A present User-Agent field line that is not valid UTF-8 cannot be matched, so the request is rejected with `custom_response_code` regardless of `allow_list` and `allow_missing_user_agent`. HTTP-family only.

blocked_patterns.description: User-Agent substrings to reject (case-insensitive). Specifying this field with an array replaces the defaults entirely. Entries are trimmed and must contain a non-whitespace character. `null` is the same as omission and installs the documented defaults. Setting the field to `[]` is valid only when `allow_missing_user_agent: false` creates a missing-header reject path; an allow-list alone is not enforcement.

allow_list.description: User-Agent tokens that always pass, evaluated before `blocked_patterns` (allow wins). Matching is case-insensitive and word-boundary anchored, so an entry only matches when it appears as a standalone token in the User-Agent. Entries are trimmed and must contain a non-whitespace character. `null` is the same as omission and installs an empty allow list.

allow_missing_user_agent.description: When true (default), requests with no User-Agent header, or only empty/whitespace-only User-Agent values, pass — this keeps health-check and load-balancer probes working. Set to false to reject them with `custom_response_code`. A non-UTF-8 User-Agent is not treated as missing and is rejected either way. `null` is the same as omission and selects `true`.

custom_response_code.description: For non-gRPC requests, the final 4xx or 5xx HTTP status returned with the JSON rejection body. Native gRPC requests instead return an empty-body HTTP 200 trailers-only error with this HTTP status mapped to `grpc-status` and `Forbidden` in `grpc-message`. Values outside 400–599, including informational and no-body status codes, and non-integer values are rejected. `null` is the same as omission and selects 403.
